newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH GROWTH TO 2010 SEEN OUTPACING OECD - ETLA.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH GROWTH TO 2010 SEEN OUTPACING OECD - ETLA.

text.p: Economic growth in Finland could outpace average growth in OECD countries until 2010, the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) said in a report received on Monday.
"Conditions exist for the Finnish national economy to continue growing at a slightly quicker pace than the average growth rate in OECD countries," ETLA said.
Assuming 2.5 percent annual growth in the OECD area, "the Finnish national economy will grow about three percent next decade," ETLA said.
Industrial production growth would be on average 3.5 percent and this would boost corporate sector investment, it said.
The share of all exports of refined metal, engineering and electrotechnical industry products would grow and Finland could increase its international market share.
Helped by export sector growth, domestic production and trade and services could also grow, ETLA said.
"Through increasing domestic demand, production of the closed corporate sector can be expected to grow in the long term at about the pace of industrial production," it said.
After the current phase of increasing demand for labour in industry, demand for labour would decrease in the longer term despite quicker output growth than the OECD average, ETLA said.
There was still scope for more new jobs in the metal, engineering and electrotechnical industry, but the forest industry and other manufacturing sectors would continue to shed jobs, it said.
New jobs could be created in sectors catering to domestic demand, but employment in these sectors would not improve to the levels before the recession in the early 1990s, it added.
The report is part of background material compiled for a government report to parliament on Finland's future.
The report will be passed to the legislature on April 29. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
